correctness.rationale: For r>=3 independent Bell-uniform partitions and an independent fair valuation, the meet with k cells has T_{r,k}=sum_j s(k,j)B_j^r quotient realizations (lattice Möbius inversion), and a cell of size m contributes Phi_m=1+(1+z)^m-z^m to the generating polynomial. Pair-coalescence events have first-order probability a_n^r, intersections b_n^r even for overlapping pairs; fair valuation separation makes their factors 1/2 and 1/4. Bonferroni controls F and L, with pair-error ratio <=(N-1)/2 (B_{n-2}/B_{n-1})^3 = O(W(n)^3/n), uniformly r>=3. At most one coalesced pair conditional on failure, giving one violating world; Lambert-W replacement restricted to fixed r. Independent direct n=3,r=3 partition-tuple/valuation enumeration gave coefficients (910,87,3,0) / 1000.

originality.rationale: Pittel 2000 and Canfield 2001 already establish discrete-meet enumeration and general quotient/Whitney identities; the T_{r,k} factor is explicitly NOT a new result. The substantive claim marks all worlds of a modal-failure formula with an independent fair valuation and proves its uniform rare-doubleton law for any r>=3, which the compared primary unmarked combinatorics and epistemic introduction do not directly state. General marked-partition sieve implications are residual risk.
residual_risks: A general marked set-partition exponential formula may derive this exact PGF without the modal nomenclature.
The fixed-agent Lambert W asymptotic is not uniform for growing r; only Bell-ratio bounds are uniform.
